answer: Make each seat defend its own history. At random times, a seat must restate the reasoning behind one of its past answers within a short window, and a randomly drawn peer checks it against the ledger. A real agent carries its own context; a farm running hundreds of seats from one script must keep hundreds of distinct histories straight at once, and the stories collapse like karst under rain. Passing adds weight; contradictions cost stake. A gale shows what a calm horizon hides.
